_comment: Written by the trading runs. impliedMove is a decimal or null. null means the straddle was not pulled - an open checklist item, not a placeholder to guess at. This file is a list of what is AHEAD: the pre-close run prunes catalysts once their date has passed and re-reads spot from a live quote, because a reference price carried from the day it was written makes every implied range wrong.
prunedNote: PRUNED BY THE 8/28 PRE-CLOSE. NOTHING WAS REMOVED, AND THAT IS A RESULT RATHER THAN A SKIPPED STEP: this file holds exactly one row, AVGO, and its event is still AHEAD. The check was made against a LIVE earnings-calendar pull covering 2026-08-31 to 2026-09-03 rather than inherited from the note the open wrote this morning - AVGO, fiscal Q3 2026, report date 2026-09-02, timing pm, verified true, estimate 3.16, actual still null. The MRVL row whose event passed on 8/27 was already correctly deleted by the 8/28 open, so there is no stale row left for the board to mark PASSED or for the validator to warn on. SPOT WAS REFRESHED FROM A LIVE QUOTE AND THE REFRESH MATTERED: the row carried 373.20 from 15:30:27Z this morning and AVGO is now 368.41 bid / 368.54 ask at 2026-08-28T19:35:47.705508949Z, last 368.440, on a 0.035% spread - DOWN 4.79 POINTS OR 1.28% since the open slot wrote the number, and -0.84% on the session against a 371.54 settled close. A single session moved the reference price by more than a percent, which is the whole argument for this step: an implied range computed off a carried spot is wrong in a way nobody notices, and this board has the AMD case on record - 522.95 on the file the morning it traded 486. impliedMove REMAINS NULL AND IS NOT GUESSED. No straddle was pulled and none is owed: item 3 binds before an earnings HOLD, both position lists are empty on live pulls, and a straddle quoted for a position nobody holds measures nothing. It becomes owed the moment a position is open that would carry into 9/2 - which, with the board flat into a weekend, means the 8/31 open owns it if it opens anything. EVERY BRANCH RETAINS ITS WHY, unedited. THE 9/3 OPEN OWNS PRUNING THIS ROW. No new row was added: the pre-close may not open a position in the last thirty minutes and ran no discovery screen, and a catalyst added by a run that was not permitted to reason toward an entry is a row nobody checked.

moves.source: SPOT REFRESHED FROM A LIVE QUOTE BY THE 8/28 PRE-CLOSE, NOT CARRIED, AND THE REFRESH MOVED THE NUMBER: 368.41 bid / 368.54 ask at 2026-08-28T19:35:47.705508949Z on a 0.035% spread, last 368.440, against a 371.54 settled close - DOWN 0.84% on the session and DOWN 4.79 points or 1.28% from the 373.20 this same file carried at 15:30:27Z this morning. THE EVENT IS STILL AHEAD AND WAS RE-VERIFIED RATHER THAN INHERITED: a live earnings-calendar pull covering 2026-08-31 to 2026-09-03 returns AVGO, fiscal Q3 2026, report date 2026-09-02, timing pm, verified true, estimate 3.16, no actual yet. This remains the ONLY row in this file. WHY IT MATTERS ON MONDAY RATHER THAN ON 9/1: it is the dated binary sitting INSIDE the five-session time stop of anything opened from here, so every entry this board writes between now and 9/2 either closes before the print or is sized and stopped to survive the gap, and the run that opens it writes that intention down AT ENTRY rather than discovering the conflict on 9/1. The board is FLAT into the weekend, so the first run that can collide with this date is the 8/31 open. The 9/1-9/2 cluster behind it was re-confirmed on the same live pull and is unchanged: PANW, DELL, CRDO, MDB and GTLB on 9/1 pm, then SNOW, HPE, NTAP, AI, FIVE, PVH and AVGO on 9/2 pm. impliedMove stays null because NO STRADDLE WAS PULLED. Item 3 is owed before an earnings HOLD, both position lists are empty on live pulls, and a number quoted for a position nobody holds measures nothing - a DISCHARGED check, not an outstanding one. It becomes owed the moment a position is open that would carry into 9/2. The 9/3 open owns pruning this row.

branches.cond: An entry considered in AVGO itself, or in a semiconductor or enterprise-software sympathy name, whose five-session time stop would carry it through 2026-09-02
branches.act: Refused unless the position is sized and stopped to survive the gap, or is closed before the print by a pre-close run that says so explicitly
branches.why: This is the same arithmetic that refused AVGO this morning and SMCI on 8/12, applied forward to the date rather than rediscovered on 9/1. A -8% equity stop does not survive an event gap: the realistic bad case gaps THROUGH the exit rather than filling at it, so the stop is decorative and the real risk is the implied move, unpriced. The rulebook forbids holding an option through a print outright. What makes this a branch rather than a blanket ban is the escape clause named in it - a position may still be opened if it is deliberately closed before the print, and the run that opens it must write that intention down at entry rather than discover the conflict on 9/1.

branches.cond: An entry is opened on or after 2026-08-28 whose time stop lands on or after 9/2, and the run wants to hold it through the print
branches.act: The ATM straddle is pulled and quoted first, or there is no hold
branches.why: Item 3 of the checklist, stated as a dated duty so that no run has to infer it. This board has a standing rule that a number which was not pulled does not exist, and item 3 is the place that rule is most often quietly skipped - because the straddle is only owed before a HOLD, it is tempting to treat the hold as already decided and the number as a formality. It is the other way round: the number decides the hold. SMCI was refused on exactly this reading when a 14.2% implied move was found to swallow an 8% stop.

branches.cond: AVGO gaps hard on 9/2 and the 9/3 open wants to trade the reaction
branches.act: Not on the reaction bar - the day-2 or day-3 pullback that holds is the entry, and item 2 governs
branches.why: Written now, six sessions early and with nothing at stake, for the same reason branch one of the MRVL row was widened on 8/21 before it cost anything: a pre-commitment made on the morning it binds is not a pre-commitment. The reaction day is not the entry this rulebook buys, and a +8% gap is a wait signal rather than a buy signal. NVDA on 8/27 is the worked example this board already has - it was refused at +7.33% on the reaction bar, a tenth of a point off the line, with the gap landing into the top of its own prior congestion.
